A struct field embedded in its struct (Go), named after its type; the reader writes every promoted field access and method call as the explicit path through it.
A newtype whose values are exactly the declared variants.
An interface type: the method signatures a value of it can be called with.
A type given a name: a basic, function, map or slice type.
the `struct` type declaration
Type parameters of a generic function, type or extern, each constrained by an interface; a method of a generic type binds its type's parameters through its receiver.
Tagged variants, each carrying its own fields.
A module-level variable: a type and an optional initializer.
A function or extern whose last parameter, a slice, takes zero or more arguments.
A call of a module function; of a generic one with `targs`, its type arguments written out, as many as it has type parameters.
A call of the function value `f`.
A declared constant or enum variant.
A conversion to the named type `name`.
A sentinel error.
A call of the function `name` of `path`, declared in the module's `externs`; with `targs`, the type arguments of a generic one, as many as its declaration has type parameters.

A call of the method `name` of the extern type `type` of `path` on `recv`, declared in the module's `externs` with that receiver type; with `targs`, the type arguments of the method's own type parameters (those of a generic receiver type are `recv`'s type's).
the `field` expression
A floating-point literal: `value` is the shortest decimal that reads back to the same number of `t`'s width, laid out as [`float_spelling`] gives it.

A module-level variable, declared in the module's `vars`; read, or assigned to on the left of an `assign`.

A call of the method `name` through `recv`, a value of the interface `iface` of `path` (empty: this module), declared in the module's `interfaces`, or a value of a type parameter that interface constrains: the method of whatever value `recv` holds runs.
the `index` expression
Type arguments written out on a call of a generic function or a use of a generic type, one per type parameter.

`sprintf`, `errorf`, `println`, `append`, `len` or `sorted_keys`. `sorted_keys` takes a map and gives its keys as a slice in ascending order: integers numerically, strings by UTF-16 code unit, as Java's String.compareTo orders them, which byte order does not always match.

A function literal. `captures` names every local, parameter or receiver of the enclosing function it reads or writes, each in scope where the literal stands; inside `body` only `captures` and `params` are in scope.
A literal in the source language's spelling.
An empty map or slice.

The value `x`, of a concrete type or of another interface, used where a value of the interface `t` is expected.

A local, parameter or receiver.

`for init; cond; post { body }`: `init` runs once, `cond` is checked before each iteration (absent: always true), `post` runs after each iteration, including one a `continue` ends. `init` is a `let` or an `assign`; `post` an `assign`, `incr` or `decr`.

intrinsic.append.note: Not claimed, though its case intrinsic-append passes. Go's compiler may give a slice that does not escape a stack buffer of another capacity than the heap growth the evaluator follows, so a program whose output depends on whether two appends share an array may print otherwise under Go.

stmt.foreign.note: Case stmt-foreign: the writer refuses it: codespec-write-cir: refused Count (case.go:6): foreign go statement: defer is outside cir/1; the evaluator stops there. A foreign statement keeps source whose meaning cir/1 does not give; the evaluator stops when it reaches one, so the writer refuses a function holding one.

stmt.raise.note: Case stmt-raise: the writer refuses it: codespec-write-cir: refused Check (case.go:12): raise: it leaves every caller up to the framework, which the evaluator does not run; the evaluator stops there. A raise leaves the function and every caller up to the framework that started it, which the evaluator does not run; it stops when it reaches one, so the writer refuses a function holding one, and the kit case's calls never reach it.
